Let $I$ be a finite nonempty set. For each $\alpha\in I$, let $H_\alpha,K_\alpha$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces. A density matrix is a self-adjoint endomorphism with nonnegative eigenvalues and trace one; it is faithful when all its eigenvalues are strictly positive. Let $p_\alpha,q_\alpha>0$ with $\sum_\alpha p_\alpha=\sum_\alpha q_\alpha=1$, let $\rho_\alpha$ be a density matrix on $H_\alpha$, let $\sigma_\alpha$ be a faithful density matrix on $H_\alpha$, and let $\chi_\alpha$ be a fixed faithful density matrix on $K_\alpha$. Form the finite orthogonal direct sums

$$\rho_A:=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in I}p_\alpha\rho_\alpha\otimes\chi_\alpha,\qquad \sigma_A:=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in I}q_\alpha\sigma_\alpha\otimes\chi_\alpha.$$

For a density matrix $\tau$, set $s(\tau):=-\sum_{\lambda_j(\tau)>0}\lambda_j(\tau)\log\lambda_j(\tau)$, with $0\log0:=0$, so entropy is in nats. For density matrices $\tau,\omega$ with faithful reference $\omega$, set $D(\tau\|\omega):=\operatorname{tr}(\tau\log\tau)-\operatorname{tr}(\tau\log\omega)$ using spectral logarithms on positive eigenvalues. Also define $H(\mathbf p):=-\sum_\alpha p_\alpha\log p_\alpha$ and $D_{\rm cl}(\mathbf p\|\mathbf q):=\sum_\alpha p_\alpha\log(p_\alpha/q_\alpha)$. Then $\rho_A$ and $\sigma_A$ are density matrices, $\sigma_A$ is faithful, and

$$s(\rho_A)=H(\mathbf p)+\sum_{\alpha\in I}p_\alpha\bigl(s(\rho_\alpha)+s(\chi_\alpha)\bigr),$$

$$D(\rho_A\|\sigma_A)=D_{\rm cl}(\mathbf p\|\mathbf q)+\sum_{\alpha\in I}p_\alpha D(\rho_\alpha\|\sigma_\alpha).$$

These are exact finite-dimensional matrix identities; no literal black-hole area, universal Ryu–Takayanagi formula, continuum limit, or gravitational entropy claim follows.

If $D_n>0$, then $D_n$ is a positive integer and $\rho_n=D_n^{-1}I$ has eigenvalue $1/D_n$ with multiplicity $D_n$. Its trace is $D_n(1/D_n)=1$, and it is self-adjoint with nonnegative eigenvalues; hence it is a density matrix by [F2]. Substitution into [F3] gives $s(\rho_n)=-D_n(1/D_n)\log(1/D_n)=\log D_n$ by [F5].

Under [A1], direct multiplication gives $N^2=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&2\end{pmatrix}=N+I$. Therefore $D_0=1$, $D_1=0$, and $D_2=1$. For every $n\geq0$, $N^{n+2}=N^nN^2=N^{n+1}+N^n$; taking the $(0,0)$ entry proves $D_{n+2}=D_{n+1}+D_n$.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unit and $\delta\in R$. For each $n\ge0$, let $F_n:=R\langle u_1,\ldots,u_{n-1}\rangle$ be the free associative unital $R$-algebra on the indicated symbols ([[lem-hh-free-associative-ring-and-relations-descent]]). When $n=0$ or $n=1$, the symbol set is empty and $F_n=R$.

Let $I_n$ be the two-sided ideal generated by

$$u_i^2-\delta u_i\quad(1\le i<n),\qquad u_i u_j-u_j u_i\quad(|i-j|>1),$$

and

$$u_i u_{i+1}u_i-u_i,\qquad u_{i+1}u_i u_{i+1}-u_{i+1}\quad(1\le i\le n-2).$$

The abstract **rank-$n$ Temperley–Lieb algebra** is the presented $R$-algebra

$$P_n(R,\delta):=F_n/I_n.$$

Thus its defining relations are $u_i^2=\delta u_i$, $u_i u_{i\pm1}u_i=u_i$, and $u_i u_j=u_j u_i$ for $|i-j|>1$. The definition of a presented $R$-algebra and its universal property are those of [[lem-hh-free-associative-ring-and-relations-descent]].

Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unit ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]) and let $\delta\in R$. The object labels are the nonnegative integers $n=0,1,2,\ldots$. For labels $m,n$, place bottom points $b_1,\ldots,b_m$ and top points $t_1,\ldots,t_n$ along the rectangle from left to right on their respective edges. Their cyclic order is $t_1,\ldots,t_n,b_m,\ldots,b_1$. When $m=n=0$, the empty matching is included.

An $(m,n)$ **diagram** is a perfect matching of these $m+n$ boundary labels which is noncrossing: there are no four labels $a,b,c,d$ in cyclic order whose matched pairs are $\{a,c\}$ and $\{b,d\}$. A picture consists of disjoint arcs realizing the matching; equality is equality of the matching, so planar deformation that fixes the boundary does not change a diagram. If $m+n$ is odd, there are no such diagrams. Write $\mathcal D(m,n)$ for this set and define the $R$-module

$$M_R(m,n):=R^{(\mathcal D(m,n))},$$

the free $R$-module on the set of diagrams ([[def-free-module-on-a-set-and-standard-basis]]). In particular, its diagram basis is empty when $m+n$ is odd.

For basis diagrams $D:m\to n$ and $E:n\to p$, stack $E$ above $D$ and identify the $n$ matching boundary points. The resulting finite graph has degree two at each identified point, where degree means the number of incident arcs. Each component is a path joining two exterior boundary points or a closed cycle. Remove every cycle and multiply the remaining exterior matching by $\delta^c$, where $c$ is the number of removed cycles. Denote this output by $E\circ D$ and extend the rule $R$-bilinearly to a map $M_R(n,p)\times M_R(m,n)\to M_R(m,p)$. A following result proves closure of these operations on the diagram modules and the category axioms.

The matching $1_n:n\to n$ pairs each bottom point to the top point directly above it. Horizontal juxtaposition, with the left diagram placed first, defines $m\otimes m'=m+m'$ on object labels and $D\otimes D'$ on basis diagrams; extend it $R$-bilinearly to the modules. A following result proves that these operations give a strict monoidal category.

For $1\le i<n$, let $d_i\in M_R(n,n)$ be the diagram with a cap joining top points $i,i+1$, a cup joining bottom points $i,i+1$, and vertical through strands at every other position. Define $\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$ to be the $R$-module $M_R(n,n)$ with bilinear multiplication $xy:=x\circ y$ and distinguished element $1_n$. A following result proves that it is a unital associative $R$-algebra and identifies it with the endomorphism algebra at object $n$.

The left factor is stacked above the right factor. The loop value is $\delta$; no invertibility or nonzero condition on $\delta$ is part of these data.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unit and $\delta\in R$. Define the quantum integers by

$$[0]_\delta=0,\qquad [1]_\delta=1,\qquad [r+1]_\delta=\delta[r]_\delta-[r-1]_\delta\quad(r\ge1).$$

The **quantum characteristic** of $(R,\delta)$ is the least positive integer $\ell$ with $[\ell]_\delta=0$, if one exists, and $\ell=\infty$ otherwise. No element of $R$ is inverted in this definition.

For $q\in\mathbb C^\times$ and $\delta=q+q^{-1}$, write $[r]_q=[r]_\delta$. If $q\ne\pm1$, this agrees with $(q^r-q^{-r})/(q-q^{-1})$; at $q=\pm1$ the recurrence gives $[r]_q=rq^{r-1}$. For complex-parameter classification, write $\kappa=\operatorname{ord}(q^2)$, with $\kappa=\infty$ when $q^2$ has infinite order. If $q\ne\pm1$, the quantum characteristic equals $\kappa$ when $\kappa<\infty$ and is $\infty$ otherwise. At $q=\pm1$, $\kappa=1$ but the complex quantum characteristic is $\infty$, because $[r]_q=rq^{r-1}\ne0$ for every positive $r$.

For a field $K$ of positive characteristic $p$, set $p(0)=1$ and, when $\ell<\infty$, set $p(i)=\ell p^{i-1}$ for $i\ge1$. In characteristic zero and finite $\ell$, the finite digit scale is $p(1)=\ell$; the separate characteristic-zero criterion below uses $a\ell-1$ for arbitrary positive integers $a$. If $\ell=\infty$, every finite index is already in the range $n<\ell$.

Fix an integer $n\geq1$ and a real loop parameter $\delta$. Define $[0]_\delta=0$, $[1]_\delta=1$, and $[r+1]_\delta=\delta[r]_\delta-[r-1]_\delta$ for $r\geq1$. Assume $[k]_\delta\neq0$ for $2\leq k\leq n$; this list is empty when $n=1$. The abstract generator algebra $P_n(\mathbb C,\delta)$ is the unital complex algebra with generators $u_1,\ldots,u_{n-1}$ and relations $u_i^2=\delta u_i$, $u_i u_{i\pm1}u_i=u_i$, and $u_i u_j=u_j u_i$ when $|i-j|>1$. The diagram algebra $\mathrm{TL}_n(\mathbb C,\delta)$ has basis the noncrossing pairings of $n$ ordered bottom and $n$ ordered top points; its product stacks the left factor above the right, deletes each closed loop, and multiplies by $\delta$ per loop. Its elementary diagram $d_i$ has a cap joining top points $i,i+1$, a cup joining bottom points $i,i+1$, and vertical strands elsewhere. The isomorphism $\Phi_n:P_n(\mathbb C,\delta)\to\mathrm{TL}_n(\mathbb C,\delta)$ sends $u_i$ to $d_i$.

For every $1\leq i\leq n-2$, the adjacent relations in the presentation mean both $u_i u_{i+1}u_i=u_i$ and $u_{i+1}u_i u_{i+1}=u_{i+1}$. For matching the imported recursion's notation, write $U_i:=d_i$.

Set $p_1=1_1$. For $1\leq r<n$, put $Q_r=p_r\otimes1_1$ by adjoining one rightmost vertical strand and define

$$p_{r+1}:=Q_r-\frac{[r]_\delta}{[r+1]_\delta}Q_r d_r Q_r.$$

The denominator hypotheses make this recursion defined. For each $1\leq r\leq n$, let $\widehat p_r:=\Phi_r^{-1}(p_r)$. The cited Jones-Wenzl result gives $p_n^2=p_n$ under these unit-denominator hypotheses. For $1\leq r\leq n$, let $\iota_{r,n}:P_r(\mathbb C,\delta)\to P_n(\mathbb C,\delta)$ send each generator $u_i$ to the same-named generator, and let $\jmath_{r,n}:\mathrm{TL}_r(\mathbb C,\delta)\to\mathrm{TL}_n(\mathbb C,\delta)$ append $n-r$ rightmost vertical strands. The maps commute with $\Phi$: on each generator, both composites send $u_i$ to $d_i$ with those added strands, and both send the unit to the identity diagram. Since generators and unit generate $P_r$, the composites agree on every element.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space. A unital representation is a unital complex-algebra homomorphism $\pi:P_n(\mathbb C,\delta)\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(H)$, where $\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(H)$ is the algebra of complex-linear endomorphisms of $H$. Require each $\pi(u_i)$ to be self-adjoint, meaning $\langle\pi(u_i)x,y\rangle=\langle x,\pi(u_i)y\rangle$ for all $x,y\in H$. Define $P:=\pi(\widehat p_n)$, define $\operatorname{rank}P:=\dim_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{im}P$, and restrict to data with $\operatorname{rank}P>0$. $$\operatorname{ptr}_n(p_n)=\frac{[n+1]}{[n]}p_{n-1},\qquad \operatorname{Tr}_n(p_n)=[n+1].$$

Only the displayed denominator units are assumed; $\delta$ need not be a unit.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $\delta\in R$, and use the noncrossing-pairing diagram category of [[def-temperley-lieb-diagram-category]], with the left factor stacked above the right factor. For a basis diagram $D:n\to n$, close each top endpoint to the corresponding bottom endpoint outside the rectangle and let $c(D)$ be the number of circles in the resulting finite graph. Define

$$\operatorname{Tr}_n(D)=\delta^{c(D)}$$

and extend $R$-linearly to $\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$. This is the **unnormalized closure trace**. In particular, $\operatorname{Tr}_0(1_0)=1$ and $\operatorname{Tr}_n(1_n)=\delta^n$. No unit or nonzero condition on $\delta$ is required.

Let $\cup:0\to2$ and $\cap:2\to0$ be the standard cup and cap in the diagram category. For $n\ge1$ define the **right partial trace** by

$$\operatorname{ptr}_n(x)=(1_{n-1}\otimes\cap)\circ(x\otimes1_1)\circ(1_{n-1}\otimes\cup),\qquad x\in\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta).$$

It is a map $\mathrm{TL}_n\to\mathrm{TL}_{n-1}$. If $\delta$ is a unit, define $\tau_n=\delta^{-n}\operatorname{Tr}_n$. This agrees with the normalized trace of [[def-temperley-lieb-normalized-markov-trace-by-closure]] over $\mathbb C$ when $\delta\ne0$.

Let $I$ be a finite nonempty index set. For each $\alpha\in I$, let $H_\alpha$ and $K_\alpha$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces, and give

$$H_A:=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in I}(H_\alpha\otimes K_\alpha)$$

the orthogonal direct-sum inner product: distinct summands are orthogonal and the inner product within a summand is the Hilbert tensor-product inner product. On elementary tensors that inner product is $\langle x\otimes y,x'\otimes y'\rangle=\langle x,x'\rangle\langle y,y'\rangle$. A map $T\otimes U$ acts by $(T\otimes U)(x\otimes y)=Tx\otimes Uy$, and a direct-sum map acts blockwise with zero off-diagonal blocks.

A complex-linear endomorphism is a linear map from a vector space to itself. These are the conventions used for the finite density matrices in the earlier modular-balance result. The summand indexed by $\alpha$ is called the $\alpha$ sector. $$\mathcal E_\chi(\mathbf p,\rho):=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in I}p_\alpha\,\rho_\alpha\otimes\chi_\alpha.$$

When this encoded endomorphism is a density matrix, call it the encoded reduced state. The logical data are $\mathbf p$ and $\{\rho_\alpha\}$; the ancillary matrices $\{\chi_\alpha\}$ are held fixed. For a second strictly positive probability vector $\mathbf q$ and faithful density matrices $\sigma_\alpha$ on the same $H_\alpha$, write $\sigma_A:=\mathcal E_\chi(\mathbf q,\sigma)$ for the encoded reference endomorphism.

This is a finite-dimensional algebraic model. The definition makes no gravitational interpretation and does not identify a matrix entropy term with a geometric area.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over $F$ and let $T:V\to V$ be
linear. Choose any ordered basis $\mathcal B$ of $V$ and define the **trace of
the endomorphism $T$** by

$$\operatorname{tr}(T):=\operatorname{tr}([T]_{\mathcal B}^{\mathcal B}).$$

This is independent of the chosen basis: matrices of the same endomorphism in
two ordered bases are similar, and similar matrices have equal trace. When
$V$ is the zero space, the empty basis gives trace $0$.

Let $I$ be a finite nonempty set. For each $\alpha\in I$, let $H_\alpha,K_\alpha$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces. derivations.claim: By [F2], $p_n^2=p_n$. The map $\Phi_n$ and the representation $\pi$ are algebra homomorphisms, so $P^2=\pi(\widehat p_n^2)=\pi(\widehat p_n)=P$.

The imported projector result [F2] gives the unnormalized closure value $\operatorname{Tr}_n(p_n)=[n+1]_\delta$, where [F3] defines $\operatorname{Tr}_n$ by closing the corresponding diagram endpoints and weighting each resulting loop by $\delta$. This is the diagram-algebra functional recorded separately from the Hilbert-space trace.
At recursion index $1$, $Q_1:=\pi(\iota_{1,n}(\widehat p_1))=I_H$ is self-adjoint because $\widehat p_1=1$.

Suppose $1\leq k<n$ and $Q_k:=\pi(\iota_{k,n}(\widehat p_k))$ is self-adjoint. By the commuting tower identity in [L1], the diagram recursion [F1] transfers under $\Phi_n^{-1}$ and $\pi$ to $Q_{k+1}=Q_k-c_kQ_k\pi(u_k)Q_k$, where $c_k=[k]_\delta/[k+1]_\delta\in\mathbb R$ because $\delta$ is real and the recurrence defines real quantum integers. Since $\pi(u_k)$ and $Q_k$ are self-adjoint, $(Q_k\pi(u_k)Q_k)^*=Q_k\pi(u_k)Q_k$, so $Q_{k+1}^*=Q_{k+1}$.
Applying the finite step 1.4 from base step 1.3 through $k=n-1$ gives $Q_n=P=P^*$; when $n=1$, step 1.3 already gives the conclusion.

For every $x\in H$, $x=Px+(I_H-P)x$, with $Px\in\operatorname{im}P$ and $P(I_H-P)x=0$, so $(I_H-P)x\in\ker P$ by [F8]. If $y=Pu\in\operatorname{im}P$ and $z\in\ker P$, then $\langle y,z\rangle=\langle Pu,z\rangle=\langle u,P^*z\rangle=0$ by step 2.1. Thus the two subspaces are orthogonal and sum to $H$, so their intersection is zero and $H=\operatorname{im}P\oplus\ker P$. The idempotent $P$ acts as the identity on $\operatorname{im}P$ and as zero on $\ker P$, so it is an orthogonal projection with eigenvalues $1$ on its $r$-dimensional image and $0$ on the kernel.

By step 3.1 and [F5], the ordinary Hilbert-space trace is $\operatorname{tr}_H(P)=r$, while step 1.2 gives the separate diagrammatic closure value. The operator $\rho=P/r$ is self-adjoint and has eigenvalues $1/r$ on $\operatorname{im}P$ and $0$ on $\ker P$. In a basis formed from bases of these subspaces its trace is $r(1/r)=1$, so it is a density matrix by [F4,F5]. Its entropy is $-r(1/r)\log(1/r)=\log r$ by [F6,F7]. This concludes the proof using the self-adjointness established by induction in step 2.1.
